By partitioning the search space and restricting lineage interaction, it prevents all lineages from prematurely collapsing onto the same local optimum, thus maintaining the very diversity required for cross-cutting explanations to eventually form through recombination.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If variance in primitive vocabularies across lineages strictly decreases over time despite ownership isolation, then the diversity-preservation mechanism is failing.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If recombination events between isolated lineages are systematically rejected by the system's allocation policy, the heuristic degenerates into permanent suppression.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a single lineage's vocabulary asymptotically covers all valid primitives without external input, ownership is redundant rather than diversity-preserving.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In a combinatorial search space, unrestricted inter-lineage communication (e.g., allowing any lineage to solve any problem) causes premature convergence: lineages rapidly synchronize on the most accessible local optimum, discarding outlier primitives that might later prove necessary for cross-cutting explanations. Ownership-based allocation forces lineages to explore disjoint regions of the primitive space. The 'suppression' of a rival lineage solving a problem is actually a temporary quarantine, preserving epistemic diversity.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
